head: GEOGRAPHICAL CONGRESS OPENS IN CAIRO
body: The International Geographical Congress opened in Cairo today under royal patronage, with delegates from many nations. It is to sit until 9 April.

head: SPECIAL STAMPS FOR THE CONGRESS
body: The Egyptian Post Office issued a set of commemorative stamps today marking the International Geographical Congress at Cairo.

head: HEBREW UNIVERSITY OPENED ON MOUNT SCOPUS
body: Lord Balfour inaugurated the Hebrew University at Jerusalem today before a large gathering that included Lord Allenby and Sir Herbert Samuel. Egypt was represented at the ceremony.

head: BALFOUR MOBBED IN DAMASCUS
body: Crowds protesting against Lord Balfour's visit clashed with police near his hotel in Damascus. Two persons were killed and eleven wounded.

head: GEOGRAPHICAL CONGRESS CLOSES
body: The International Geographical Congress ended its Cairo sittings today after nine days of meetings.

head: LORD BALFOUR LEAVES DAMASCUS
body: After two days of disturbances, Lord Balfour was taken out of Damascus by motor and conveyed to the Lebanon under escort.

head: BALFOUR SAILS FOR ALEXANDRIA
body: Lord Balfour embarked at Beirut aboard the steamer Sphinx, bound for Alexandria and Marseilles.

head: NEW JEWISH COLONY IN PALESTINE
body: Immigrants from Poland founded the settlement of Givat HaShlosha in Palestine today.

head: LUTFI AL-SAYYID EXPLAINS JERUSALEM VISIT
body: Ahmad Lutfi al-Sayyid defended and apologised for his attendance at the opening of the Hebrew University in Jerusalem, where he had represented the Ziwar Government. His presence there has drawn sharp criticism in the Cairo press.

head: HEJAZ: PILGRIM SHIPS TO LAND AT RABIGH
body: The Mecca newspaper Umm al-Qura announced that Indian pilgrim ships would land at Rabigh, and that special provision had been made for pilgrims' safety while Jeddah remains under siege.

head: NEW LABOUR DAILY IN PALESTINE
body: The first number of Davar, a Hebrew daily newspaper, appeared in Palestine today.

head: SIRDAR MURDER: DEATH SENTENCES PASSED
body: The Cairo court trying the assassins of Sir Lee Stack pronounced sentences of death today. The case has been followed closely since the Sirdar was shot in Cairo last November.

head: LORD ALLENBY LEAVES EGYPT
body: Lord Allenby, who resigned as High Commissioner in May, has left Egypt after six years in office. At Port Said crowds burned an effigy of him.
note: Wikipedia gives only 'resigned May 1925' and the Port Said effigy; 14 June taken from an Arabic 'on this day' post (Facebook, King Farouk page) naming 14 June 1925 for Allenby's resignation/leave-taking. Unconfirmed day.

head: SIR HERBERT SAMUEL ENDS TERM IN PALESTINE
body: Sir Herbert Samuel completed his five years as High Commissioner for Palestine today.

head: SYMES ACTING IN JERUSALEM
body: Colonel G. S. Symes took charge as acting High Commissioner for Palestine pending the arrival of Lord Plumer.

head: MECCA REPORTS PILGRIMAGE ENDED
body: Umm al-Qura reported the close of this year's pilgrimage season and delays to pilgrim shipping. Egypt sent no official caravan this year.
note: Source gives the date of the Umm al-Qura report; the 'no Egyptian caravan' clause rests on the same article mentioning the Egyptian edict against the 1925 Hajj (no exact date).

head: DRUZE CHIEFS EXILED TO PALMYRA
body: General Sarrail has arrested Druze sheikhs who came to state their grievances and banished them to Palmyra. Unrest is reported in the Jebel Druze.

head: FRENCH COLUMN DESTROYED IN JEBEL DRUZE
body: Druze fighters under Sultan al-Atrash destroyed a French relief column at al-Kafr; over a hundred French soldiers are reported killed.

head: PALESTINIAN CITIZENSHIP ORDER IN FORCE
body: The Palestinian Citizenship Order came into force today, granting Palestinian citizenship to former Ottoman subjects resident in the country.

head: HEAVY FIGHTING AT MAZRAA
body: A strong French column under General Michaud has been attacked by Druze and Bedouin horsemen at al-Mazraa in the Hauran. Fighting continues.

head: FRENCH ROUTED AT MAZRAA
body: The French column in the Jebel Druze has been driven back with severe losses after two days' fighting at al-Mazraa.

head: AL-AZHAR EXPELS SHEIKH ALI ABD AL-RAZIQ
body: The Council of Senior Ulama, presided over by the Rector of al-Azhar, has struck Sheikh Ali Abd al-Raziq from the ranks of the ulama over his book 'Islam and the Principles of Government'. The hearing lasted some forty minutes.

head: DRUZE AND FRENCH EXCHANGE PRISONERS
body: French and Druze prisoners were exchanged at Umm Walad in the Hauran after negotiations opened between the mandatory authorities and the Druze leaders.

head: SIRDAR'S ASSASSINS EXECUTED
body: Seven men condemned for the murder of Sir Lee Stack were hanged in Cairo this morning. The bodies are to be handed to their families on condition that there be no demonstrations at the burials.

head: SULTAN AL-ATRASH PROCLAIMS REVOLT
body: The Druze leader Sultan al-Atrash has issued a call to all Syria to rise against the French mandate.

head: LORD PLUMER TAKES UP PALESTINE POST
body: Field-Marshal Lord Plumer assumed office today as High Commissioner for Palestine and Transjordan.

head: MINISTER OF JUSTICE DISMISSED
body: Abd al-Aziz Fahmi Pasha, Minister of Justice, has been dismissed over the affair of Sheikh Ali Abd al-Raziq's book. He had declined to act on al-Azhar's ruling against the author.

head: PRESS BATTLE OVER FAHMI DISMISSAL
body: The newspapers continue their fierce dispute over the dismissal of the Minister of Justice. The British High Commission is reported to have intervened.

head: FRENCH WITHDRAW FROM SUWAYDA
body: French forces have withdrawn from al-Suwayda, capital of the Jebel Druze, leaving much of the town in ruins.

head: RISING IN HAMA
body: Insurgents rose in Hama against the French on the night of 4 October. French aircraft are reported bombing the town.

head: DAMASCUS BOMBARDED
body: Rebel bands under Hasan al-Kharrat entered Damascus. From six this evening French artillery and aircraft have been shelling the city.

head: DAMASCUS SHELLING CEASES
body: The French bombardment of Damascus ended about noon today after some eighteen hours. Great damage is reported in the old city.

head: LORD LLOYD ARRIVES
body: Lord Lloyd, the new British High Commissioner, has arrived to take up his post in succession to Lord Allenby.
note: No source found giving the day. Sources confirm only that his term began in 1925; the user's brief says arrival Oct 1925. 21 Oct is a best guess. DOUBTFUL; verify before use.

head: NEW WEEKLY: ROSE AL-YUSUF
body: The actress Fatima al-Yusuf has brought out the first number of her new weekly magazine 'Rose al-Yusuf'.

head: TUTANKHAMUN'S GOLDEN FACE REVEALED
body: At Luxor Mr Howard Carter raised the lid of the innermost coffin today, revealing the king's mummy with a mask of solid gold.

head: GENERAL SARRAIL RECALLED
body: The French Government has recalled General Sarrail, High Commissioner in Syria, following the bombardment of Damascus.

head: NEJD-TRANSJORDAN FRONTIER AGREED
body: Sir Gilbert Clayton and Sultan Ibn Saud signed agreements at Hadda and Bahra settling questions of the frontier between Nejd and Transjordan.

head: EXAMINATION OF THE PHARAOH BEGINS
body: In the Valley of the Kings, Dr Douglas Derry began the examination of the mummy of Tutankhamun this morning in the presence of Mr Carter and Egyptian officials.

head: TUTANKHAMUN EXAMINATION COMPLETED
body: The scientific examination of Tutankhamun's mummy was completed today. The doctors estimate the king was about eighteen years old at death.

head: DRUZE ATTACK RASHAYA
body: Druze rebels under Zayd al-Atrash have attacked the French garrison at Rashaya in the Lebanon. The garrison is holding out.

head: DEPUTIES MEET IN DEFIANCE OF GOVERNMENT
body: Members of the dissolved Chamber gathered in Cairo on the constitutional opening day of Parliament and elected Zaghlul Pasha President, although the Government had closed the Parliament building.
note: The user's brief names 21 Nov 1925 (Continental Hotel). 21 Nov 1925 was the third Saturday of November, the day the 1923 Constitution fixes for Parliament to meet; no web source seen states the day. Treat as probable, not confirmed.

head: RASHAYA RELIEVED
body: After four days of fighting, French aircraft and a relief column have raised the siege of Rashaya. The Druze have withdrawn to the Anti-Lebanon.

head: ZIWAR PASHA TAKES INTERIOR PORTFOLIO
body: The Prime Minister, Ahmad Ziwar Pasha, has taken over the Ministry of the Interior in addition to the premiership.
note: Source gives his Interior tenure as 30 Nov 1925 to 7 Jun 1926.

head: M. DE JOUVENEL IN BEIRUT
body: The new French civilian High Commissioner, M. Henry de Jouvenel, has arrived in Beirut and received large delegations. 'Peace to those who want peace; war to those who want war,' he declared.
note: TIME issue of 14 Dec 1925 says he arrived 'last week'; the exact day is not given.

head: MEDINA SURRENDERS TO IBN SAUD
body: The garrison of Medina surrendered the city to the Nejdi forces this morning. Prince Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz is to enter tomorrow.
note: Sabq gives Saturday 19 Jumada I 1344 = 5 Dec 1925. Other pages give 3 or 9 Dec.

head: JAGHBUB CEDED TO ITALY
body: Ziwar Pasha signed the agreement with Italy fixing Egypt's western frontier and handing the oasis of Jaghbub to Italian Libya.

head: ELECTIONS FOR JEWISH ASSEMBLY
body: Jewish voters in Palestine elected the second Assembly of Representatives today.

head: NEW ELECTORAL LAW DECREED
body: The Government has issued a decree-law amending the electoral law. The opposition parties condemn it.

head: MOSUL AWARDED TO IRAQ
body: The Council of the League of Nations has awarded the greater part of the Mosul vilayet to Iraq, over strong Turkish objections.

head: KING ALI GIVES UP THE HEJAZ
body: King Ali of the Hejaz has abdicated. His reign ends as Jeddah prepares to hand itself over to Ibn Saud.

head: LAKE TSANA NOTES EXCHANGED
body: Britain and Italy completed in Rome an exchange of notes on a barrage at Lake Tsana and an Italian railway across Abyssinia. The Lake Tsana project touches the waters of the Blue Nile.

head: JEDDAH SURRENDERS; SIEGE ENDS
body: The siege of Jeddah is over and the city has been handed over to Sultan Ibn Saud. The Hashemite kingdom of the Hejaz is at an end.

head: TUTANKHAMUN TREASURES TO CAIRO
body: The gold mask and other objects from the tomb of Tutankhamun have been removed from Luxor to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo.
note: Source gives only 'December 1925'. Day is a placeholder.

head: IBN SAUD PROCLAIMED KING OF THE HEJAZ
body: At the Great Mosque of Mecca, Sultan Abd al-Aziz ibn Saud of Nejd was proclaimed King of the Hejaz and received the oath of allegiance.

head: NEW ANGLO-IRAQI TREATY
body: Britain and Iraq have signed a new treaty extending their relations for twenty-five years or until Iraq joins the League of Nations.
note: Toynbee's Survey gives 13 Jan 1926; Wikipedia's January 1926 page gives 19 Jan.

head: OPPOSITION PARTIES FORM JOINT COMMITTEE
body: The Wafd, the Liberal Constitutionalists and the National Party have set up a joint executive committee to settle a common line towards the King and the Ziwar Government.

head: SENNAR DAM OPENED
body: The great dam on the Blue Nile at Makwar near Sennar was formally opened today. It will water the cotton lands of the Gezira. Lord Lloyd performed the ceremony.
note: OAC confirms the 21 Jan 1926 official opening; Lord Lloyd as opener is from a SuperStock photo caption.

head: GIZA QUEEN'S TOMB REOPENED
body: Dr Reisner's Harvard-Boston expedition reopened the sealed burial chamber found at Giza last year near the Great Pyramid, to begin systematic clearance.

head: PALESTINE-SYRIA GOOD-NEIGHBOUR AGREEMENT
body: British and French representatives signed an agreement of friendship on behalf of the Palestine and Syria-Lebanon mandates.

head: PRINCE FAISAL VICEROY OF THE HEJAZ
body: Prince Faisal, son of King Ibn Saud, has taken office as Viceroy of the Hejaz.

head: INDEPENDENCE ANNIVERSARY
body: Egypt marks four years since the British declaration of 28 February 1922 ending the Protectorate.
note: Anniversary item: the date is fixed, but no source says how it was marked in 1926.

head: RUTENBERG GETS JORDAN POWER CONCESSION
body: The High Commissioner for Palestine has granted Mr Pinhas Rutenberg an exclusive seventy-year concession for the Palestine Electric Corporation.

head: KING FUAD'S BIRTHDAY
body: His Majesty King Fuad I turns fifty-eight today.
note: Anniversary item from his birth date, 26 Mar 1868; no source for 1926 celebrations.
